# PR #3523: Patch: a dungeon run's time counts only while it is played, so a run picked up the next day is not timed by the calendar

Closes #3502

## What changed

A dungeon run's time is now the time it was played, not the calendar's. A run played 5 minutes, left 10 hours and played 5 more settles at 10 minutes, and the on-screen timer shows the same total.

- **Kept time.** `KeptRun` gains `elapsedMs`, the time played as of the last save. `startedAt` is still kept but no longer times the run.
- **Session clock.** The new `Live.resumedAt` is when the session on screen began, or null while paused. It is never stored. `playedMs(elapsedMs, resumedAt, now)` is `elapsedMs` plus the session since, with each session slice floored by `DUNGEON_ELAPSED_MIN_MS` (a clock set back adds nothing).
- **When it banks.**
  - Every save (`step`) adds the session to `elapsedMs`.
  - So do `visibilitychange` to hidden, `pagehide`, and the last Dungeon page unmounting ("Back to Play").
  - `visibilitychange` to visible and `pageshow` (back-forward cache) resume the clock.
- **Reload.** A reload folds the kept run and starts a new session from the kept total.
- **Older kept runs.** A run with no `elapsedMs` starts at the new `DUNGEON_ELAPSED_START_MS = 0` when it loads. A run whose `elapsedMs` is not a non-negative integer is dropped, like any other malformed kept run.
- **Settling.** A settled run is never written back to storage: `setSession` returns early for finished runs.
- **`Dungeon` type.** `startedAt` is replaced by `elapsedMs` and `resumedAt`. `RunTimer`, `RunHud` and `FightScreen` pass them through, and `RunTimer` shows `playedMs(...)`.
- **Ruling R3502000.** Its note proves itself in `store.test.ts` and `RunTimer.test.tsx`. Its §11 paragraph is in `spec/pending/3502.md` and its §15.10 sentence is in `spec/15-dungeon-run.md`. `docs/dungeon-run.md` (the `Dungeon` listing and B24) is updated too. I did not run `cargo jackioh spec index`.

- **`pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/dungeon`:** 11 files, 114 tests passed.
- **`store.test.ts`:** I updated 4 existing assertions. The new `R3502000` tests (all with a fake clock) cover:

  - a page that opens hidden;
  - a back-forward-cache restore;
  - leaving the Dungeon page;
  - an older kept run, and bad-shape `elapsedMs` values (-5, 1.5, "10", null) being dropped;
  - the floor, including a clock set back after a banked 5 minutes;
  - a settled run not being kept again on hide.
- **`RunTimer.test.tsx`:** the B24 test uses the new props, plus the "reload shows the kept total" and "paused timer holds the total" tests.

  - `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`: clean.
  - `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/dungeon`: clean.

  - `cargo fmt --check`: ok.

## Decisions the issue left open

- **Start screen counts.** The clock runs while the Dungeon page is open, including the start screen's Continue wait. Rejected: pausing it until Continue, which would wire `DungeonPage`'s `entered` state into the store.
- **Leaving the page stops the clock.** Rejected: timing only hide and `pagehide`, which would time a tab left open on another route.
- **`startedAt` stays in storage** and is removed from `Dungeon`. Rejected: reusing it as a "virtual start".
- **No `DUNGEON_STORAGE_VERSION` bump.** A bump would drop every kept run, so `elapsedMs` is optional on read.

- **Cleanup path.** In `subscribe`'s cleanup I call `setSession(onScreen())` where the plan says `setSession(false)`. It pauses when the last listener leaves and does nothing while another remains, which is simpler when a screen swap briefly drops the listener count.

- **Test reloads.** `reload()` calls `cleanup()`, which pauses and banks up to the current clock. A test that moves the clock to model a closed page must dispatch `pagehide` first. The B19 test and the 10-hour test do.

  - `onStorage` replaces this tab's unbanked session with the other tab's copy.
  - All three undercount and none overcounts. I left them unhandled, as the plan accepts.
- **Campaign runs.** The Campaign's server-checked runs (§15.12) will need their own time rule, and R3502000's note says so.

# #3502: Patch: a dungeon run's time counts only while it is played, so a run picked up the next day is not timed by the calendar
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The dungeon keeps a "fastest win" board and shows a running timer. A run can now be left and picked up later, but the timer counts the hours you were away. Finish a run you paused overnight and your win is recorded as taking twenty hours, and the on-screen timer says the same. Once this is built, a run's time counts only while the run is open on your screen, as most roguelikes time a run.

## Why

- **The recorded time is wall-clock time.** `apps/web/src/dungeon/store.ts:357` gives a settled run `timeMs: Math.max(DUNGEON_ELAPSED_MIN_MS, now - live.startedAt)`. `startedAt` is kept with the run and restored on reload (`store.ts:93`, `store.ts:155-160`).
- **The on-screen timer uses it too.** `apps/web/src/dungeon/fight/RunTimer.tsx:20-34` counts from the same `startedAt`.
- **It feeds a leaderboard.** §15.10 (`spec/15-dungeon-run.md:251`): "Leaderboards: deepest row, most curse points, top score and fastest win, with an on-screen timer." The fastest board ranks by `timeMs` (`DungeonStats.test.tsx:237-252`).
- **Leaving and coming back is now normal.** #3476 (R2972000) made it the expected path.

## Proposal

- **Keep the time played.** `KeptRun` gains `elapsedMs`.
  - The store adds the current session's time on every save, and when the page is hidden or closed (`pagehide`, `visibilitychange`).
  - A reload starts a new session from the kept total, not from `startedAt`.
  - Time while the tab is hidden does not count.
- **The timer shows the same total.** `RunTimer` shows the kept total plus the running session.
- **Older runs.** A kept run from before this change has only `startedAt`; it starts its count at the moment of the change, so no earlier gap is counted again.
- **Spec and ruling.** A ruling for what a run's time counts: Hearthstone has no run timer, so it follows the roguelike convention of time played. It gets its note and pending paragraph, and §15.10 says it.

## Where it lands

- `apps/web/src/dungeon/store.ts` and `store.test.ts`
- `apps/web/src/dungeon/fight/RunTimer.tsx` and its test
- spec §15.10

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A store test with a fake clock: a run played 5 minutes, left 10 hours, reloaded and played 5 more minutes settles with 10 minutes.
- [ ] Time while the page is hidden is not counted; time before a `pagehide` is.
- [ ] After a reload, `RunTimer` shows the kept total.
- [ ] `DUNGEON_ELAPSED_MIN_MS` still floors the recorded time.
- [ ] The ruling's note, test and pending paragraph are in place, and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.

## Size and risks

Small: about 4 files plus the ruling. Difficulty medium.

- What counts as a run's time is a design call the maintainer may prefer to make differently.
- The Campaign's server-checked runs (§15.12, not built yet) will need a rule of their own.
- "A dungeon run in progress survives a card patch" (suggested alongside this one) also edits `KeptRun`, so build the two in turn.
